I know that sounds like some slut biker gang and hopefully it will be soon but for now I'm contemplating taking a few clones which means that I'll be growing a few moms for awhile, all of which I've yet to attempt, so I'm wondering how to go about things in a practical manner.

Soil seems easy and while I can make up a decent mix, it's still always a pain, invites pests and so on. It'd require its own feeding schedule, suffer its own deficiencies, and monopolize my time in its own way which I find counter productive if it has to be a hassle at all. There are reasons why I'm using hydroponics in the first place and it seems like they aren't worthy of compromise on the basis of keeping a few small moms.

For the cloning portion, I've already got a few suckers nearly raised up enough for taking at any time but I'm going to let them go longer so they have more of a head start. After I cut them, I'll score their ends, give them a quick dip in honey, roll them in cloning powder, stuff them Rapid Rooters and then in freezer bags for a humidity dome.

For the more interesting part:

A passive shallow water culture setup using fabric air pruning pots sitting in a tray holding a shallow nutrient solution about a half inch max in depth. The fabric pot will be filled with expanded clay pellets that I already have and since they lack sufficient wicking ability on their own there will be an additional distributed wicking system added, and this is the brilliant part, cut chunks of rapid rooters used to fill the majority of interstitial spacing. It'll essentially be a large rapid rooter (think of it as a sponge) but with far superior drainage air holding capacity.

This experimental setup should be "self watering" and will be self pruning in the root zone such that it won't get rootbound or require repotting. It will also allow regular feeding using the exact same nutrient solution that the existing hydro setup uses, thereby not generating any new work to maintain it at all other than grabbing a cup of nutrient stew and tossing it into the tray every so often. While it is primarily a wicking system, and like government a bottom feeding one, the heavy drainage capacity will also allow it to be well flushed on a regular basis which it may require as salts may concentrate within the media based on constant evaporation over an extended period of time.

I think it should work perfectly and will be an affordable, hassle free way to keep a mom hydroponically without generating any extra work, mess, noise, or great expense. As a bonus, the entire "mom" could be picked up and transferred directly into the bioponic system at any time given that the media is basically the same, ensuring full compatibility.
